risks: Minimal: anonymised records; practices may feel judged, so practice results go first to each practice and are published without names.
consent: Individual consent is not required for anonymised extracts under the network governance note; practices consent through data release agreements.
data: Extraction on practice premises into an anonymised form; postcode district converted to deprivation quintile at extraction; no names or dates of birth leave the practice.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: adults in deprived areas are more likely to have no interval recorded and may be most harmed by both over-long and absent recall; missing intervals are reported by deprivation, and the result is framed so that longer intervals do not become a reason to reduce access in deprived areas.
effectiveness: Gives commissioners a baseline of whether recall is risk-based before contracts change.
efficiency: Six months of part-time research time; no practice payments.
partnerships: Practice managers, the local dental committee, commissioners and two patient representatives.
rebPath: Research ethics review not required for anonymised record extracts (network governance note PBRN-GOV-2026-11); extraction waits for signed data release agreements from all 14 practices, the unmet gate on the accepted decision.
limitations: Recorded risk is unreliable; one month; 14 practices.
summary: Anonymised records with practice-first reporting and equity reporting by deprivation.
